bull.probability_evidence: Reverse DCF shows the price implying -2.6% year-1 revenue growth against actual 11% Q1 FY27 bookings growth and a raised 9-11% FY27 guide [fact sheet Fair value; Q1 FY27 transcript], the valuation re-rating case, but conviction was capped at 3/5 because of leverage (3.17x) and the unexplained September drop, so only 25% weight is put on a clean re-rate (evaluation Bear/Bull cases).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Fair value table: DCF-base 44.28 vs EV/Revenue-base 37.89 (research/GEN/2026-10-09-valuation.md) are the two anchors underlying this scenario's own basis text, 'consistent with the mechanical base fair value of 42.15'; half the 6.40 spread (3.20) / target 42.0 = 7.6%.

base.probability_evidence: Base case is the modal outcome: guided 9-11% growth holds (Q1 FY27 transcript) with only partial multiple recovery (P/FCF 8.8x toward 5y median 13.5x) because 3.17x leverage and Altman Z 1.42 [ST,RA] cap the re-rating within 12 months (evaluation Decision JSON scenarios.base.basis).

jumps.name: Quarterly earnings reaction miss
jumps.reason: Next earnings is Nov 5, 2026; GEN's weekly history shows large reactions to quarterly reports in both directions (e.g. -10.69% the week of the Q3 2024 release), and the bear case explicitly ties the thesis to whether guided 9-11% growth is confirmed or missed at the next print.
jumps.cite: fact sheet Price: 'Next earnings date Nov 5, 2026' [ST,OV]; note §3 Valuation ties the thesis to Q1 FY27 bookings/guidance; evaluation Bull case basis

annual_probability.cite: Quarterly reporting cadence: mc-inputs event_weeks lists exactly 4 earnings-release weeks per year in GEN's history, so a given earnings-reaction week occurs with probability 1 (one jump per quarter modelled); the single-event probability per year used here is 4 occurrences/yr, expressed as an annual hazard of 1 (set at 0.25 per quarterly event to match the 4/yr cadence with this impact size).

jumps.name: Leverage / credit-stress re-rating
jumps.reason: Net debt/EBITDA is 3.17x TTM and Altman Z is 1.42, in the distress zone; the note flags that capital return (buybacks/dividends) is competing with deleveraging rather than being purely additive, a risk distinct from the gradual multiple compression already built into the bear scenario's target.
jumps.cite: note §2 Quality and §6 Unusual items: 'Altman Z of 1.42 (distress zone) alongside 3.17x net leverage is a balance-sheet risk factor' (research/GEN/2026-10-09.md); fact sheet Other: Net debt/EBITDA 3.17x, Altman Z 1.42 [ST]

annual_probability.cite: No company-specific credit/refinancing event appears in GEN's 5-year weekly history (0 analogues in mc-inputs event_weeks), so a low base rate is set given the distress-zone Altman Z of 1.42 [ST] but still-tight, not-yet-stressed credit backdrop (HY spread 3.09%, macro overlay).

impact.cite: assumed, within the ±30% bound for an unanalogued jump

jumps.assumption: No dated credit-stress analogue exists in GEN's own weekly history (event_weeks contains only earnings/proxy/M&A dates, no credit event); impact is assumed from the magnitude of the 'distress-zone' leverage risk the note and fact sheet flag, kept at |0.20| < the 0.30 cap for an unanalogued jump.

jumps.name: Repeat of an unexplained single-week price shock
jumps.reason: The stock fell from a 31.65 high (2026-09-03) to a 20.34 low (2026-09-29) and 'neither the note nor the fact sheet explains why'; short interest is elevated at 7.80% of float and rising (+1.5% m/m). This models the risk of another such abrupt, uncatalysed single-week move -- distinct from the bear scenario's target, which instead assumes the de-rating becomes a sustained, fundamental P/FCF compression to 7.0x.
